title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Dow fell Friday for a third straight losing week even as the S&P 500 edged up on a chip rally and the Nasdaq gained 0.4%; the 10-year Treasury yield briefly topped 5% (settling at 4.995%) on oil-driven inflation bets, while WTI crude tumbled ~6.5% to ~$95.

Markets: Bitcoin topped $81,000 and crypto extended gains into the weekend - Layer-2/DeFi tokens like Starknet and Arbitrum jumped 17%+ - as post-Fed-hike nerves faded and the 10-year yield slipped back below 5%.
Markets: The yen sank to about 157.8/dollar even after the Bank of Japan hiked rates, as investors read the move as more cautious than hoped for a stronger yen.
Companies: Warren Buffett stepped down as Berkshire Hathaway chairman, handing the seat to son Howard effective immediately (Buffett stays on the board as chairman emeritus; Greg Abel remains CEO).

Companies: Coinbase jumped ~12%, the S&P 500's top gainer, after filing for regulatory approval to list perpetual futures tied to individual U.S. stocks; Netflix fell >3% on a Wells Fargo downgrade, and Steel Dynamics/Nucor slid on weak Q3 guidance.
Companies: SpaceX's Nasdaq-100 weighting is set to more than double, to about 2.82% from 1.28%, in Friday's quarterly index rebalance, effective Monday Sept. 21.

Macro/Policy: The Fed raised rates 25bp to 3.75%-4.00% on Sept. 16 - its first hike since 2023 - citing inflation running above target despite a steady labor market, with another hike this year still possible.
Macro/Policy: The Bank of Japan raised its policy rate 25bp to 1.25%, the highest since 1995, continuing to accelerate its normalization campaign.
